andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh declares 388 mandals drought-affected across 21 districts
facts: The Andhra Pradesh Revenue (Disaster Management) Department issued drought declaration GO No. 4 on 1 October 2026 for the 2026 kharif season.
The declaration covers 388 mandals in 21 districts: 283 severely affected and 105 moderately affected.
Rainfall from 1 June to 31 August was reported as 197.6 mm against a normal 424.3 mm, a 53.4% deficit.
The order was issued ahead of the usual 31 October kharif declaration date, citing the rainfall deficit and prevailing El Niño conditions.
The drought-affected districts include Srikakulam, Anakapalli, Krishna, Palnadu, Markapuram, Kurnool, Anantapuramu, YSR Kadapa and Annamayya.
andhraPradesh.summary: A state government order dated 1 October classified 388 mandals across 21 districts as drought-affected, including 283 severe and 105 moderate cases. The declaration was made early for the kharif season amid a reported 53.4% June–August rainfall deficit.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Drought assessment and management; agricultural vulnerability and disaster relief.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the declaration totals—388 mandals in 21 districts, comprising 283 severe and 105 moderate—and the reported June–August rainfall deficit of 53.4%.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how timely drought classification can support relief planning and agricultural resilience, while noting the need for transparent crop-loss assessment and water-security measures.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct AP development: the order covers mandals in 21 Andhra Pradesh districts.

andhraPradesh.headline: Five additional judges appointed as permanent judges of the Andhra Pradesh High Court
facts: The President appointed five additional judges as judges of the Andhra Pradesh High Court through orders notified on 1 October 2026.
The appointees are Justices Maheswara Rao Kuncheam (also reported as Kuncham), Thoota Chandra Dhana Sekar, Challa Gunaranjan, Avadhanam Hari Haranadha Sarma and Yadavalli Lakshmana Rao.
The appointments were made under Article 217(1) of the Constitution.
The appointments take effect from the date each judge assumes office.
andhraPradesh.summary: On 1 October, the Department of Justice listed the appointment order for five additional judges of the Andhra Pradesh High Court as permanent judges. The appointments are under Article 217(1) and take effect when the judges assume office.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Constitutional provisions on appointment of High Court judges; structure of the Indian judiciary.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Article 217(1) provides for the appointment of High Court judges by the President; the 1 October 2026 notification covered five Andhra Pradesh High Court judges.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Relate judicial appointments to constitutional procedure, continuity in High Court functioning and the importance of addressing judicial vacancies.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct AP connection: all five appointments are to the Andhra Pradesh High Court.

national.headline: GOBARdhan scheme launched to expand India’s compressed biogas sector
facts: Union Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri launched the GOBARdhan Central Sector Scheme on 1 October 2026.
The Union Cabinet approved it on 6 August 2026 with an outlay of ₹23,731 crore for FY 2026–27 to FY 2035–36.
The scheme combines assured offtake, administered pricing, capital assistance, pipeline connectivity and credit support for compressed biogas (CBG).
The CBG procurement obligation for City Gas Distribution entities is 3% in FY 2026–27, 4% in FY 2027–28 and 5% from FY 2028–29 for CNG transport and domestic PNG segments.
Eligible greenfield projects may receive capital assistance of up to ₹2 crore per tonne per day of installed CBG capacity.
A Unified GOBARdhan Portal and scheme handbook were launched to support implementation.
national.summary: The launch operationalises a national framework intended to scale up compressed biogas production and use organic waste as a clean-energy feedstock. Its procurement obligations, price support and infrastructure assistance connect waste management with energy security and rural economic activity.
national.staticLink: Circular economy, bioenergy, waste-to-wealth and clean-energy policy.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Remember GOBARdhan’s ₹23,731-crore outlay, ten-year period, CBG procurement obligation schedule and its links to City Gas Distribution entities.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how predictable offtake, finance and gas-evacuation infrastructure can help convert agricultural and organic waste into a commercially viable circular bioeconomy.

national.headline: UPSC marks its centenary with commemorative releases and a case-law compilation
facts: The Union Public Service Commission marked 100 years at a centenary event held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 1 October 2026.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the event.
A commemorative postage stamp, a special coin and the book “100 Landmark Judgements—Shaping the Policies of UPSC and Public Service Commissions in India” were released.
The occasion highlighted the Commission’s role in public-service recruitment and the constitutional framework for Public Service Commissions.
national.summary: The centenary event recognised UPSC’s institutional history and its place in India’s public-administration framework. The stamp, coin and case-law compilation were released as commemorative materials; the event was not a change to the Commission’s constitutional mandate.
national.staticLink: Constitutional bodies; Union and State Public Service Commissions; Articles 315–323.
national.prelimsTakeaway: UPSC’s constitutional framework is covered by Articles 315–323; the Commission marked its centenary on 1 October 2026.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how an independent merit-based recruitment institution contributes to administrative neutrality, competence and public trust.

national.headline: Centre revises sugar dealers’ stock limits from 15 October
facts: The Centre announced revised sugar stock-holding norms on 1 October 2026, the start of the new sugar season.
From 15 October to 30 November 2026, dealers may hold no more than 1,000 quintals and may not retain stock for longer than 15 days from receipt.
The stated exceptions are Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas, and Assam.
The measure is intended to support availability and reasonable consumer prices during the festive period.
national.summary: The government announced time-limited stock controls for sugar dealers as the new season began. The limits take effect on 15 October 2026, so they were announced on 1 October but were not yet operational on that date.
national.staticLink: Essential commodities, food-price management and the Centre’s regulatory role in markets.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The announced limit is 1,000 quintals, with a maximum holding period of 15 days; the notified period begins 15 October 2026.
national.mainsAngle: Examine the trade-off between temporary stock controls to discourage hoarding and the need for predictable, efficient food-supply chains.

sources.title: Government Revises Sugar Stock Holding Norms to Prevent Hoarding and Ensure Smooth Supply to Consumers During Festive Season

national.headline: Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff marks 25 years of jointness and integration
facts: Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) marked 25 years since its establishment on 1 October 2001.
The Silver Jubilee was observed in New Delhi on 1 October 2026, designated in the release as Tri-Service Day.
The event included “Trishakti Manthan” under the theme “Future readiness through jointness & Integration”.
The discussions covered joint operational doctrines, joint training, integrated exercises and coordination of humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.
national.summary: The anniversary drew attention to HQ IDS’s role in coordination among the armed services and in advancing joint operational preparedness. The event also linked defence integration with the planning and coordination needed for humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.
national.staticLink: Higher defence organisation, civil-military coordination and disaster-response preparedness.
national.prelimsTakeaway: HQ IDS was established on 1 October 2001; its 25th anniversary event in 2026 used the theme “Future readiness through jointness & Integration”.
national.mainsAngle: Explain how joint doctrines, training and integrated exercises can improve the effectiveness of tri-service operations and disaster response.

national.headline: National Voluntary Blood Donation Day observed with nationwide campaign
facts: National Voluntary Blood Donation Day 2026 was observed on 1 October at Lady Hardinge Medical College, New Delhi.
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s Blood Transfusion Services Division organised the national observance with the college and its associated hospitals.
The 2026 theme was “One Drop of Humanity. Give Blood. Save Lives.”
A nationwide mega voluntary blood-donation campaign was scheduled from 17 September to 2 October 2026.
The campaign promoted regular, voluntary and non-remunerated donation; e-RaktKosh was used for donor registration and monitoring.
national.summary: The observance focused on building a regular voluntary donor base and ensuring a safe, adequate supply of blood and blood components. The nationwide campaign was scheduled to continue through 2 October 2026.
national.staticLink: Public-health systems, blood-transfusion services and community participation in health.
national.prelimsTakeaway: National Voluntary Blood Donation Day is observed on 1 October; the 2026 theme was “One Drop of Humanity. Give Blood. Save Lives.”
national.mainsAngle: Discuss the role of voluntary, non-remunerated blood donation and digital coordination in strengthening equitable and reliable health services.

sources.title: National Voluntary Blood Donation Day 2026 Observed with Renewed Call for Regular Voluntary Blood Donation
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

national.headline: ICAR and FCI sign research MoU on safer foodgrain storage
facts: The Indian Council of Agricultural Research and the Food Corporation of India signed the MoU on 30 September 2026; PIB reported it on 1 October.
The two-year Phase-I project will research alternative fumigation technologies for managing storage pests in wheat and rice.
ICAR–Central Institute of Post-Harvest Engineering and Technology, Ludhiana, will implement the project.
The Department of Food and Public Distribution supports the research.
The project aims to support safer and more sustainable foodgrain storage.
national.summary: The MoU establishes a research project on alternatives to conventional fumigation for pests in stored wheat and rice. It is a research collaboration, not a completed technology deployment or a change to national foodgrain-storage rules.
national.staticLink: Food security, post-harvest management and agricultural research institutions.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The ICAR–FCI MoU covers alternative fumigation research for wheat and rice; Phase I is two years and implemented by ICAR-CIPHET, Ludhiana.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how post-harvest research can reduce storage losses while addressing pest resistance, chemical use and food-security needs.

sources.title: ICAR and FCI signs MoU for Safe and Sustainable Foodgrain Storage

national.headline: Fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave announced for New Delhi
facts: The Ministry of Finance announced the fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave on 1 October 2026.
The conclave was scheduled for 3–5 October 2026 in New Delhi under the theme “Resilience in an Age of Flux”.
It is an initiative of the Institute of Economic Growth, organised in partnership with the Ministry of Finance.
The announced programme was to bring together more than 180 participants, including over 80 international participants from around 30 countries.
The event was scheduled to discuss economic resilience, global fragmentation, technology, trade, finance and India’s economic priorities.
national.summary: The announcement set out the fifth edition’s dates, theme and partnership between the Institute of Economic Growth and the Ministry of Finance. As of 1 October, the conclave was upcoming; no outcomes should be treated as having been reached on that date.
national.staticLink: Macroeconomic policy, economic resilience and international economic cooperation.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave was announced for 3–5 October 2026 in New Delhi; its theme was “Resilience in an Age of Flux”.
national.mainsAngle: Consider how economic policy can build resilience to global shocks while sustaining growth, investment and institutional credibility.

international.headline: G20 trade ministers condemn using food trade as geopolitical coercion
facts: G20 trade ministers met in Milwaukee, United States, from 30 September to 1 October 2026, under the U.S. G20 Presidency.
Ministers issued a statement condemning coercive measures that use trade in food, agricultural products or inputs to seek unrelated geopolitical concessions.
The discussions also covered global excess capacity, the WTO most-favoured-nation principle and forced labour in supply chains.
India’s Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal participated in the meeting.
Food-security implications include possible disruption to agricultural supply chains and harm to vulnerable populations.
international.summary: The G20 Trade Ministerial concluded in Milwaukee on 1 October with a statement condemning the weaponization of food through coercive trade actions. India participated in discussions on the global trading system and food security; the statement is not a binding trade agreement.
international.staticLink: G20 as a forum for international economic cooperation; WTO principles and global food security.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the host city, dates, four discussion areas and the distinction between a ministerial statement and a binding treaty.
international.mainsAngle: Assess how trade restrictions can affect food security and the rules-based trading system, while considering the policy space of developing countries.

international.headline: NASA–SpaceX Crew-13 launches four-person crew to the International Space Station
facts: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 mission launched on 1 October 2026 from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida.
The launch vehicle was a SpaceX Falcon 9 carrying a Dragon spacecraft to the International Space Station (ISS).
The crew comprised NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov.
The mission supports research aboard the ISS, including studies involving stem-cell-derived tissues, plant growth and astronaut health.
The spacecraft launched for an ISS science expedition; NASA lists the mission as active.
international.summary: Crew-13 launched to the ISS on 1 October, continuing the station’s multinational human-spaceflight and research programme. The mission is part of NASA’s commercial crew partnership with SpaceX and includes astronauts from the United States and Canada and a cosmonaut from Russia.
international.staticLink: International Space Station, multinational space cooperation and commercial human-spaceflight programmes.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Crew-13’s launch vehicle was Falcon 9 and its spacecraft was Dragon; the destination is the ISS.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss how public–private partnerships and international cooperation sustain low-Earth-orbit research and contribute to future human exploration.

international.headline: Greece assumes the rotating presidency of the UN Security Council for October
facts: Greece held the rotating presidency of the 15-member UN Security Council for October 2026.
Under the Council’s provisional rules, its presidency rotates monthly among members in English alphabetical order.
The presidency is a procedural leadership role and does not give Greece additional Council membership or voting rights.
The United Nations confirmed Greece’s October 2026 presidency in its official schedule.
international.summary: Greece’s one-month Security Council presidency began on 1 October 2026. The presidency oversees the Council’s programme of work and meetings, while the Council’s membership and voting rules remain unchanged.
international.staticLink: UN Security Council composition, functions and monthly rotating presidency.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The Security Council presidency rotates monthly among Council members in English alphabetical order.
international.mainsAngle: Explain how the Security Council’s rotating presidency shapes its agenda-setting and working methods without changing the formal powers of its members.

international.headline: UN marks International Day of Older Persons under the theme “The Age of Longevity”
facts: The United Nations observes the International Day of Older Persons annually on 1 October; 2026 marked its 36th observance.
The 2026 theme was “The Age of Longevity: Rethinking Systems for Longer Lives.”
The UN projected that the global population aged 60 and over would rise from 1.2 billion to 2.1 billion by 2050, reaching 20% of the world population.
The observance highlighted the need for policies addressing health care, pensions, housing, employment, lifelong learning and age discrimination.
international.summary: The UN’s 2026 observance focused on adapting social and economic systems to longer lives and ageing populations. Its theme links healthy ageing and dignity with social protection, participation and intergenerational solidarity.
international.staticLink: Population ageing, social security, healthy ageing and the rights and welfare of older persons.
international.prelimsTakeaway: International Day of Older Persons: 1 October; 2026 theme: “The Age of Longevity: Rethinking Systems for Longer Lives.”
international.mainsAngle: Examine the challenges of population ageing and propose an inclusive policy response spanning health care, income security, housing and protection from discrimination.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the Andhra Pradesh drought declaration for the 2026 kharif season?
options: It covers 388 mandals in 21 districts, including 283 severely affected and 105 moderately affected mandals.
It covers 283 mandals in 21 districts, including 105 severely affected and 178 moderately affected mandals.
It covers 388 mandals in 15 districts, all classified as severely affected.
It covers 105 mandals in 21 districts, all classified as moderately affected.
mcqs.explanation: GO No. 4 declared 388 mandals drought-affected across 21 districts: 283 severe and 105 moderate.

mcqs.question: The Andhra Pradesh drought order reported rainfall from 1 June to 31 August as:
options: 197.6 mm against a normal 424.3 mm, a 53.4% deficit.
424.3 mm against a normal 197.6 mm, a 53.4% surplus.
197.6 mm against a normal 283 mm, a 30% deficit.
105 mm against a normal 388 mm, a 53.4% deficit.
mcqs.explanation: The order cited 197.6 mm of rainfall against a normal 424.3 mm, representing a 53.4% deficit.

Up to ₹2 crore per project, regardless of installed capacity.
Up to ₹23,731 crore per tonne per day of installed CBG capacity.
Up to ₹5 crore per project for the entire scheme period.
mcqs.explanation: Eligible greenfield projects may receive capital assistance of up to ₹2 crore per tonne per day of installed CBG capacity.
